description: Replay a bounded finite-state Metropolis-Hastings chain with an asymmetric proposal matrix and exact rational draw tape.

source.algorithm: W. K. Hastings, Monte Carlo sampling methods using Markov chains and their applications
source.role: The Archive chapter names Metropolis-Hastings as an extension. Hastings (1970) supplies the asymmetric proposal correction; the bounded integer profile is independently specified.

input.encoding: [N, T, initial, weights[N], Q[N*N], proposals[T], (draw_numerator, draw_denominator)[T]]
input.proposal_validity: For each step, Q[current_state, proposed_state] must be positive under the simulated current state.

output.encoding: The state trace, one byte per state ID: initial state followed by one resulting state per proposal.
output.error_precedence: Validate the full input and simulate into a local trace before checking output pointer/capacity.

workspace.meaning: Fixed staged trace buffer, so invalid inputs and short/null output buffers leave caller output untouched.

algorithm_details.acceptance: For current x and proposal y, let numerator=weight[y]*Q[y,x] and denominator=weight[x]*Q[x,y]. Accept if numerator>=denominator; otherwise accept exactly when draw_num*denominator < draw_den*numerator.
algorithm_details.proposal_probability: Q[i,j]/1024; the shared row denominator cancels from the Hastings ratio.
algorithm_details.self_proposals: Accepted because their Hastings ratio is one.
algorithm_details.zero_reverse_probability: If Q[y,x] is zero, reject the proposal.
algorithm_details.integer_bound: Each target and proposal entry is at most 1024, so a Hastings product is at most 1024^2. Each cross product includes one draw component bounded by 1024, so all compared values are at most 1024^3=1,073,741,824, safely within signed 64-bit.
algorithm_details.complexity: O(N*N + T) time and O(T) fixed staging space.
algorithm_details.determinism: The proposal states and exact rational variates are supplied. The profile benchmarks their deterministic replay and makes no mixing or convergence claim.

references.primary: Primary oracle applies the exact cross-product acceptance comparison for each supplied transition.
references.independent: Independent oracle derives a rational acceptance cutoff for each directed state pair, constructs the exact transition kernel, verifies detailed balance, then replays the supplied trace using Fraction comparisons.
